name: @wave-av/mcp-server
purpose: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes WAVE as tools for AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf): 25 tools spanning streams, studio productions, analytics and billing, the voice/transcribe/captions product spokes, WAVE Dispatch model routing, and the public x402/MPP agent-payment rails.

capabilities.does: List all streams in the WAVE account with pagination and status filtering.
Create a new stream (protocol, recording, region options).
Start a stream by ID, transitioning it to the active state.
Stop an active stream by ID.
Get real-time stream health metrics (bitrate, frame rate, latency).
List all studio productions in the WAVE account.
Create a new multi-camera studio production.
Get current viewer count and viewer demographics for a stream or account-wide.
Get detailed stream performance metrics (bitrate, latency, quality, error rates).
Get current subscription plan, billing cycle, and feature entitlements.
Get current billing-period usage (streaming minutes, storage, bandwidth).
Switch the live program output to a different camera/source in a Cloud Switcher session.
Create a clip from a recorded stream, optionally exporting to social platforms.
Show, hide, or update an HTML5 graphics overlay on a production.
Control a PTZ camera (pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall/store).
Moderate a chat message in a live stream (block, flag, or allow).
Start real-time captions/transcription on a stream.
Mark a moment in a stream as a highlight for later clipping.

Synthesize speech from text via POST /v1/voice. Returns a receipt — content type, size, and billed usage — rather than the audio itself, since an MCP tool result is a text block and raw audio cannot travel through one.
Transcribe audio from a publicly reachable URL via POST /v1/transcribe, returning the JSON transcript. Optional engine (auto/whisper/deepgram/elevenlabs), language hint, and speaker diarization.
Generate a caption file from audio at a URL via POST /v1/captions, returning WebVTT, SubRip, or JSON cues as text.

Classify a prompt with WAVE Dispatch and return the model route it selected plus the reasoning, so an agent can pick the cheapest capable model instead of hardcoding one. Calls Dispatch on its own host, not the product gateway.
List WAVE Dispatch's named routing profiles (Fast / Expert / Heavy / Code). Feature-flagged server-side, so it can legitimately report as unavailable in a given environment.
Semantic search over WAVE's MPP directory for machine-payable services an agent can buy from. Public: no API key is sent, because the route takes none.

List the payment schemes and networks WAVE's x402 or MPP facilitator supports, so an agent settles on a scheme WAVE accepts. Public: no API key is sent. Only the read half of the rails is exposed — verify and settle are deliberately not wrapped as tools.

claims.text: Server connects via stdio transport (no network listener)
The payment-rail tools send no Authorization header, because those gateway routes are public and a key sent to them would leak for no benefit
The voice/transcribe/captions paths come from each spoke's own router, not from api-spec/openapi.yaml, which over-declares endpoints that 404 in production

sections.heading: Setup
sections.body:
### 1. Get an API key

```bash
# Via CLI
wave auth login

# Or create at https://wave.online/settings/api-keys
```

### 2. Configure your AI tool

Add to your `.mcp.json` (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) — see the Quick start config above.

sections.body:
Access WAVE entities directly via the `wave://` URI scheme:

- `wave://streams/{id}` - Stream configuration and status
- `wave://productions/{id}` - Studio production details

sections.heading: In-process (Claude Agent SDK) mode
Setup for other AI tools
Troubleshooting
sections.body:
### Server not starting

Verify your API key is set:

```bash
echo $WAVE_API_KEY
```

### Tools not appearing

Restart your AI tool after adding the MCP configuration. Most tools require a restart to detect new MCP servers.

### Connection errors

The MCP server uses stdio transport (no network listener). If you see connection errors, check that `npx` can run successfully:

```bash
npx @wave-av/mcp-server --version
```

### Testing the server

Send a JSON-RPC initialize request to verify:

```bash
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1.0.0"}}}' | npx @wave-av/mcp-server
```
